overview: An apoenzyme is the inactive protein part alone; a holoenzyme is the complete, catalytically active enzyme with its cofactor attached.
genZNote: Apoenzyme: the engine without fuel. Holoenzyme: engine plus fuel, ready to actually run.

aspects.label: Catalytic Activity
aspects.valueA: Inactive on its own — the protein component alone.
aspects.valueB: Fully active — the complete functional enzyme.

aspects.label: Composition
aspects.valueA: Protein portion only, lacking its non-protein cofactor/coenzyme.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Inactive carbonic anhydrase without its zinc ion.
aspects.valueB: Carbonic anhydrase with its zinc ion bound, fully functional.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Holoenzyme = Apoenzyme + Cofactor is a direct, exam-friendly equation.
overlay.commonMisconception: An apoenzyme is not a different enzyme — it's the same protein, just missing its essential non-protein partner.
